answer: At a digital wharf where agents trade lotus seeds, dispute votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight, so a crowd of fake agents is a hollow advantage. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital and losing its use elsewhere for the full escrow period.
